title: Polynomials: zeros & coefficients
examples: Teacher, how do I find the zeros if the polynomial is factored?
What does the degree of a polynomial really tell us?
Can I use the sum and product rules if the polynomial has more than three zeros?

explain.say: Today we are learning about polynomials and their zeros. A zero is an x value that makes the polynomial equal to zero.
The degree of a polynomial is the highest power of x in the expression. For example, in three x cubed plus two x, the degree is three.
If a polynomial has a zero at x equals two, then we know that (x minus two) is a factor. This is a key relationship to remember.

draw.text: Zero at x=c means (x-c) is a factor

explain.say: We can use the division algorithm to check for zeros. If we divide the polynomial by (x minus c) and the remainder is zero, then c is a zero.

faq.q: How many zeros does a polynomial have?
faq.a: A polynomial of degree n has exactly n zeros, counting multiplicity. This is known as the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra.
asks: What is the maximum number of zeros?
Does the degree tell me the number of zeros?

faq.q: If I know two zeros, how do I start building the polynomial?
faq.a: If you know two zeros, say c and d, you can start by multiplying the factors (x minus c) and (x minus d).
asks: How do I use two zeros to make a polynomial?
What is the first step when given two roots?

faq.q: What are the sum and product of the zeros for a general polynomial?
faq.a: For a polynomial a x squared plus b x plus c, the sum of the zeros is negative b divided by a. The product is c divided by a.
asks: Formula for sum and product of roots?
How do I find the sum of the zeros quickly?

faq.q: What does the remainder theorem help me with?
faq.a: The remainder theorem tells us that when a polynomial is divided by (x minus c), the remainder is equal to P(c).
asks: What is the remainder when dividing by (x-c)?
Does the remainder equal the zero?

faq.q: Can I find the zeros just by looking at the graph?
faq.a: Yes, the zeros are the x-coordinates where the graph crosses or touches the x-axis. These points are where y equals zero.
asks: Where do I find the zeros from a graph?
What does the graph tell me about the zeros?

facts: The degree of a polynomial is the highest exponent of the variable.
If c is a zero, then (x minus c) is a factor of the polynomial.
For a quadratic ax squared plus bx plus c, the sum of the zeros is negative b divided by a.
The division algorithm states that P(x) = Q(x) D(x) + R(x).

quiz.say: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x squared minus 3x plus one?
quiz.why: The highest power of x in this polynomial is x squared, so the degree is two.

wrong.0: This is tempting because there are three terms, but the degree looks at the highest power.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the highest power present is x squared, not x cubed.
wrong.2: This is incorrect because the degree is determined by the exponent, not the coefficient.

quiz.say: If a polynomial has zeros at x equals one and x equals three, what is one possible factor?
quiz.why: Each zero corresponds to a factor, so we multiply (x minus one) by (x minus three).

wrong.0: This only uses the zero at x equals one and ignores the zero at x equals three.
wrong.1: This uses the opposite signs for the factors, which would mean the zeros are at x equals negative one and x equals negative three.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because it assumes the factors are (x-3) and (x+3).

quiz.say: For the polynomial x squared plus 5x plus 6, what is the product of its zeros?
quiz.why: For ax squared plus bx plus c, the product of the zeros is c divided by a, which is six divided by one.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because it only considers the constant term without dividing by the leading coefficient.
wrong.2: This is a common mistake because students might confuse the product with the negative of the middle coefficient.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the sum of the zeros is negative b divided by a, not just b divided by a.
